node.label: Jeremy Black
node.date_label: The English Press in the Eighteenth Century (1987) · A Military Revolution? (1991) · Rethinking Military History (2004) · The British Seaborne Empire (2004)
node.description: A historian of warfare, British politics and the uses of history. The existing participant-editor reading of the military-revolution debate places him among critics of its conventional chronology, emphasizing continuity and later change. In his own written Sonshi interview he describes a comparative military history that challenges a restricted Western frame and resists a rigid separation between strategy and policy. Both arguments are scoped: the first is mediated by Clifford J. Rogers, the second is Black’s self-description, and neither establishes a single settled explanation of global military change.
